title: Protecting Consumers From SIM-Swap and Port-Out Fraud
summary: In this document, the Wireline Competition Bureau (Bureau) announces that the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has approved, for a period of three years, the information collection associated with the Commission's rules adopted in the SIM Swap and Port-Out Fraud Order, FCC 23-95. This document is consistent with that Order, which stated that the revised rules would not become effective until OMB completed its review of any information collection requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act and that the Bureau would announce the compliance date for the revised rules by subsequent Public Notice and cause the Commission's rules to be revised accordingly.

title: Modernizing to Electronic Payments
summary: FAA proposes to modernize its payment systems to require electronic payments and eliminate the option to pay by paper payment methods such as cash, money orders, and paper checks. This proposal complies with Executive Order 14247 titled "Modernizing Payments To and From America's Bank Account," which seeks to increase the efficiency of the Federal Government by phasing out paper receipts and mandating electronic payments to and from agencies.

title: In the Matter of TRISO-X, LLC; Confirmatory Order Modifying License
summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a Confirmatory Order to TRISO-X, LLC (the licensee), as a result of a successful Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mediation. On June 9, 2026, the NRC notified the licensee of an apparent violation being considered for escalated enforcement. The apparent violation involved the implementation of management measures to ensure the design basis supporting the structural stability function of the TX-1 process building's main force resisting system (MFRS) was maintained during construction. The NRC provided the licensee with the opportunity to respond through a written response, a Pre-decisional Enforcement Conference (PEC), or ADR. The licensee elected to participate in ADR, and mediation sessions were held on July 29 and August 20, 2026, during which the parties reached an Agreement in Principle. As part of the agreement, the licensee committed to taking certain corrective actions and consented to the issuance of a Confirmatory Order to make those commitments legally binding and resolve the apparent violation without further enforcement action by the NRC. The Confirmatory Order is effective upon issuance.

title: Hardwood and Decorative Plywood From the People's Republic of China, Indonesia, and the Socialist Republic of Vietnam: Countervailing Duty Orders

title: Chartering and Field of Membership for Federal Credit Unions; Associational Common Bonds and Client-Customer Relationships
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule to amend its criteria for determining associational common bonds. The amendments clarify that requiring members to buy a good, product, or service from a group as a condition of membership will no longer automatically bar eligibility as a recognized association. After considering public comments, the Board finalizes the proposed rule with certain modifications. The Board's revisions detail how NCUA assesses client- customer relationships (including relevant examples). These changes also simplify NCUA's process for reviewing pre-approved groups.

title: Modernizing the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act Rules
summary: In this document (Order), the Federal Communications Commission ("Commission" or "FCC") takes action to cut through outdated and unnecessary burdens that have slowed deployment of critical communications networks. These reforms restore balance to the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) implementation by providing clear and predictable rules to ensure NEPA serves as a tool for informed decision-making rather than a barrier to investment, innovation, and connectivity.

title: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
summary: The Department of Labor (Department or DOL) proposes to amend its regulations regarding the certification of job opportunities offered by employers seeking to employ aliens on a permanent basis in the United States. This Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM or proposed rule) strengthens the standards by which the Department receives and reviews employers' applications for permanent labor certification and improves the integrity of the overall employment-based immigrant visa program to more effectively protect the wages and job opportunities of U.S. workers similarly employed in the United States. Among the issues addressed in this proposed rule are eliminating further administration of Schedule A, which exempts certain job opportunities from the statutorily required labor market test; strengthening the minimum standards of recruitment to ensure all employers seeking labor certification access the broadest pool of high-quality U.S. workers using the latest technologies and methods; enhancing safeguards for U.S. workers impacted by layoffs, including those laid off by employers using third-party staffing companies and establishing standards for employers to report layoffs; expanding requirements for employers to provide U.S. workers with notice of filing (NOF) applications for permanent labor certification; improving employer compliance with program requirements and consideration of qualified U.S. workers that is comparable to job opportunities for which permanent labor certification is not required; and codifying the Department's practice of electronically receiving, processing, and issuing final determinations on employer requests for prevailing wages and permanent labor certifications. The changes in this proposed rule are consistent with the Secretary of Labor's (Secretary) statutory responsibilities to certify that there are not sufficient workers in the United States who are able, willing, qualified, and available to fill the petitioning employer's job opportunity at the time of application for a visa and admission to the United States, and that the employment of such alien will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed workers in the United States.

title: Takes of Marine Mammals Incidental to Specified Activities; Taking Marine Mammals Incidental to the Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission's Marine Facilities Replacement Program in North Puget Sound, Washington
summary: NMFS, upon request from the Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission (State Parks), issues this final rule and associated 5-year letter of authorization (LOA) pursuant to the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA) to govern the taking of marine mammals incidental to construction activities conducted in support of the Marine Facilities Replacement Program (MFRP) in North Puget Sound in Western Washington (WA) over the course of 5 years. This final rule prescribes permissible methods of taking and other means of effecting the least practicable adverse impact on marine mammal species and their habitat and establishes requirements for monitoring and reporting such taking.

Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) Leverage Availability
summary: The U.S. Small Business Administration ("SBA" or "Agency") is publishing this interim final rule ("IFR") amending the U.S. Small Business Administration's loan guarantee regulations applicable to the Small Business Investment Company ("SBIC") program to implement the provisions of the Investing in All of America Act of 2025 ("the Investing Act"). These provisions increase the maximum amount of leverage available to SBICs issuing standard debentures in ratios of up to two-to-one against private capital, update the private capital definition to include certain government-sponsored corporations and college/university trusts or endowments, and grant Small Business Investment Companies access to additional "bonus" leverage for investments in critical technology areas, small manufacturers, rural areas, and low-income geographic areas, all in conformance with the Investing Act.

title: Rulemaking To Provide That N-acetyl-L-cysteine Is Not Excluded From the Dietary Supplement Definition
summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is proposing to issue a regulation finding that N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) is not excluded from the dietary supplement definition in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). This action, if finalized, would allow products containing NAC to be lawfully marketed as dietary supplements, provided that such products are not otherwise in violation of the FD&C Act. We also propose to provide that the addition of NAC to a dietary supplement is not a prohibited act under section 301(ll) of the FD&C Act.

title: Marine Mammals; Proposed Incidental Harassment Authorization for the Southern Beaufort Sea Stock of Polar Bears During Exploration Activities in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge 1002 Area Alaska; Draft Environmental Assessment
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act from the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA), propose to authorize nonlethal incidental take by harassment of small numbers of Southern Beaufort Sea (SBS) polar bears (Ursus maritimus) for 1 year from the date of issuance of the incidental harassment authorization (IHA). The applicant requested this authorization for take by harassment that may result from activities associated with a seismic exploration program in the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Section 1002 area. This proposed authorization, if finalized, will be take of polar bears associated with the specified activities, which may come from the SBS stock. We invite comments on the proposed IHA and accompanying draft environmental assessment from the public, Tribes, and local, State, and Federal agencies.
